policy: These original registered probes are separate from the 56 fixed M05 tasks. No answer is shown before a saved attempt. Unfamiliar means unexposed in the recorded history, not a promise that the learner has never seen it elsewhere. Exposure/repetition, assistance and timing must be recorded. Probe results do not automatically clear any module. Once exposed, request a new independently reviewed variant.

schedule.basis: Product scheduling choices, not validated memory estimates; a check attempted immediately is not delayed evidence.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P01@1.prompt: Four labelled states r1,r2,b1,b2 have a known joint report table. Their masses with report R are (2/25,2/25,1/50,9/50), and with report N are (1/50,8/25,9/50,3/25). The label r means red; b means blue. A report R has already arrived. Take pays 30 currency units in red and −18 in blue, then charges a fee c≥0 currency units; wait pays0 with no fee. Maximize conditional expected money. Validate the law, recover the four state masses and color fibres, compute P(R) and P(red|R), derive the full legal c-domain/action rule including equality, and refute a uniform-counting shortcut on the displayed report atoms. State the conditioning/report and criterion assumptions.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P02@1.prompt: Events A,B have known probabilities7/20 and11/20; no joint law or independence is supplied. Let x=P(A∩B). Policy X pays7−20·1_{A∩B}, while Y pays1 always. Construct all four atom masses as functions of x, derive the exact feasible interval, and exhibit laws at both endpoints. Derive expected values and the criterion-dependent choice including ties. Under maximin over all compatible joint laws choose a policy. Refute the claim that marginal probabilities justify multiplying them.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P03@1.prompt: Draw two cards uniformly without replacement from four labelled cards A1,A2,B,C; every ordered pair of distinct labelled cards has probability1/12. The card color map sends A1,A2 to A and fixes B,C. Play pays4 if exactly one drawn color is A, and −2 otherwise, then charges fee c≥0. Wait pays1. Derive the law of the success event from labelled outcomes/fibres, calculate the unconstrained expected-money action rule including ties, and then impose P(net payoff<0)≤1/4. Identify all feasible choices for every c≥0 and compare them. Explain why a uniform law on distinct displayed color pairs is invalid.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P04@1.prompt: Run a capped experiment: stop at the first H, or after trial3 including trial3. P(H on trial1)=1/2; conditional on the history T, trial2 has H probability1/4; conditional on TT, trial3 has H probability3/4. An H by the cap pays4; no H pays−4. Each trial actually run costs1; a fixed outside option pays1. List disjoint terminal prefixes and exact masses, prove normalization, compute expected trial count and net payoff, compute the probability of a strictly negative net payoff, and choose under expected money. Explain why neither equal terminal-prefix weights nor one identical-trial probability is justified; do not claim the given stopping policy is globally optimal.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P01@1.reference: The eight masses are nonnegative and sum1. State masses(.1,.4,.2,.3); red fibre{r1,r2}, blue{b1,b2}. P(R)=9/25, red∩R=4/25, so P(red|R)=4/9. Conditional take=30(4/9)−18(5/9)−c=10/3−c. Legal c≥0; take when0≤c<10/3, either action atc=10/3, wait whenc>10/3. Counting two red-report atoms and two blue-report atoms gives1/2 incorrectly because their masses differ. The joint reporter law, already observed report, net fee and expected-money criterion are explicit assumptions.

rubric.criterion: Joint normalization, state masses and color fibres are correct.
Report mass9/25 and conditional red probability4/9 are derived.
Conditional net value10/3−c and legal c≥0 are correct.
Action regions and the tie at10/3 are complete.
The counting shortcut is refuted using unequal masses and model/criterion limits are explicit.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P02@1.reference: Atom masses for A∩B,A∩Bᶜ,Aᶜ∩B,Aᶜ∩Bᶜ are x,7/20−x,11/20−x,1/10+x. Nonnegativity gives0≤x≤7/20; both endpoint laws are valid. EV(X)=7−20x ranges0 to7; EV(Y)=1. For a known x choose X forx<3/10, either at3/10, Y forx>3/10. Worst compatible X value0 is below Y=1, so maximin choosesY. Independence would impose x=77/400, but it is not implied by the marginals.

rubric.criterion: Four atom masses and their normalization are constructed.
Sharp interval[0,7/20] and both endpoint laws are justified.
Expected values and their exact ranges are derived.
Known-law action threshold3/10 with tie and maximin choiceY are distinguished.
The independence multiplication is rejected as an extra assumption.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P03@1.reference: Exactly one A occurs in8 of12 labelled ordered pairs, hence success2/3. EV(play)=2−c versus wait1; play for0≤c<1, either atc=1, wait forc>1 under the unconstrained criterion. For0≤c≤4, failures have negative payoff and successes nonnegative, so loss probability1/3; forc>4 every play payoff is negative, so loss probability1. Thus play violates the1/4 constraint for every c≥0; wait is feasible and chosen. Displayed color pairs have unequal fibre sizes: AB has2 labelled preimages while BC has1, so a uniform color-pair law is false.

rubric.criterion: Success mass2/3 is derived from the12 equiprobable labelled ordered pairs.
EV2−c and legal fee domain are correct.
Unconstrained threshold1 including tie is derived.
Loss probabilities1/3 for0≤c≤4 and1 forc>4 exclude play under the1/4 constraint.
Wait is feasible and the unequal-color-fibre shortcut is refuted.

T22V3::T22E-TRD01::S24-P04@1.reference: Terminal prefixes H,TH,TTH,TTT have masses1/2,1/8,9/32,3/32, summing1. Expected count=(1/2)+2(1/8)+3(12/32)=15/8. Net payoffs3,2,1,−7 give expected net11/8; equivalently gross13/4 minus cost15/8. OnlyTTT has negative net payoff, with probability3/32. Expected-money comparison11/8>1 favors the specified experiment. The branch probabilities differ and are conditional on reachable histories; terminal prefix lengths/masses differ. This evaluates the fixed policy, not an optimization over stopping policies.

rubric.criterion: The four disjoint terminal prefixes and masses normalize.
Expected trial count15/8 is derived from the terminal law.
Terminal net payoffs and expected net11/8 are correct.
Strict loss probability3/32 and expected-money comparison with1 are correct.
Unequal-prefix/identical-probability errors are rejected and no global policy-optimality claim is made.
